discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers showed theoretically (1998) that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters, turning Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a concrete programme. Bloch and Greiner observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (2002), the first controlled realisation of a strongly correlated lattice model, and went on to develop quantum gas microscopes that image and manipulate single atoms at single lattice sites. This revealed antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localisation, string order and entanglement entropy directly. Their work established analogue quantum simulation as a new experimental approach to condensed-matter questions that are hard to solve in solids. It also laid the technical foundations for today's neutral-atom quantum processors, including atom-by-atom control and site-resolved readout. Few developments in the past quarter century have changed atomic and condensed-matter physics this much.
